The author means that the best leader does not try to be a hero. Such a person helps others to do the work and doesn't ask for praise. I fully agree with this idea because a real leader should support people, not just give orders.

My opinion is that this approach is very wise. Firstly, it makes people feel important and responsible. When a leader trusts his team, people work harder. Secondly, it helps the team to become stronger. This is because people learn to solve problems by themselves. A good leader is like a coach who stays in the background.

A good example of this is the story "The Captain's Daughter" by Alexander Pushkin. The main character, Pyotr Grinyov, shows this kind of leadership. When he arrives at the Belogorsk fortress, he doesn't act like a boss. He treats the Cossacks and ordinary soldiers with respect. He listens to their advice and helps them. Because of this, when the fortress is in danger during Pugachev's rebellion, the people trust him. They feel that they are protecting their home together. Grinyov doesn't take all the credit; he lets the people feel that their courage saved the day.

To sum up, I believe that the greatest leaders don't need to be in the spotlight. All things considered, the true art of leadership is to guide people so well that they feel they achieved success themselves. That is why I think this quote is completely right.
